newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian dairy giant to import 10,000 heifers.
newsitem.headline: Croatian dairy giant to import 10,000 heifers.

text.p: Croatian private dairy group Lura plans to import 10,000 heifers as part of its efforts to boost domestic production and reduce dependence on imported milk, a company executive said.
Some 5,000 heifers alone will be imported by Dukat, Croatia's biggest milk factory in which Lura has a 85-percent stake, Dukat director Ivan Purgar told Privredni Vjesnik.
With majority stakes in two other dairies apart from Dukat -- Sirela Bjelovar and Mljekara Zadar -- Lura controls some 70 percent of the Croatian market.
Purger said Dukat plans to increase pre-tax profit by some 6.5 percent this year. The 1996 pre-tax profit was 19 million German marks, on a turnover of some 240 million marks,
The company, which processed some 110 million litres of milk in 1996, plans to reduce milk imports to 11 from 17 percent of the total needed for this year's production, Purgar said.
He said the company received some 15 offers from Auastria, Germany and the Netherlands, with prices ranging between 1,800 and 2,400 German marks per heifer.
Dukat will distribute the heifers to its partners who will pay them off through milk deliveries.

Dukat now buys milk from more than 16,000 farmers, who produce on average some 13.6 litres a day each, but it plans to cut costs by reducing the number of farmers it uses, increasing at the same time their productivity. --Davor Huic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
